featured.title: Meta Just Made a CRED Founder the Boss of WhatsApp. The Real Prize Is the 500 Million Indians Who Already Live There.
featured.excerpt: Kunal Shah, who built CRED into India's slickest fintech, takes over the world's biggest messaging app alongside Meta's $900 million bet on his company. The job is to finally make WhatsApp pay — and India is the test lab.
featured.image_caption: CRED founder Kunal Shah, named global head of WhatsApp. The real prize is the 500 million Indians already on the app (Wikimedia Commons)
featured.nri_angle: Most NRIs run their entire Indian lives through WhatsApp — family groups, the neighbourhood kirana, airline alerts — so a payments-and-commerce overhaul led by a founder who understands Indian consumer behaviour will reshape how the diaspora moves money and shops across borders.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: After Nearly Two Years, India Reopens Its Doors to Bangladeshi Tourists
news.excerpt: From June 28, Bangladeshis can once again apply for Indian tourist visas at five centres across the country, ending a suspension that began amid the 2024 upheaval. The thaw is the clearest sign yet that ties between the two neighbours are mending.
news.image_caption: Tourists at the Taj Mahal in Agra. India will resume issuing tourist visas to Bangladeshi nationals from June 28, 2026, ending a nearly two-year suspension.
news.nri_angle: India's decision to resume tourist visas for Bangladeshi nationals from June 28, after a nearly two-year suspension, signals a thawing of relations that resonates across the eastern subcontinent's diaspora — families straddling the India-Bangladesh frontier, and the large Bangladeshi-origin communities in Britain, the US, Canada and the Gulf with relatives on both sides, can again plan the cross-border visits for weddings, funerals and reunions that had been tangled in geopolitics since 2024.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Europe Is Living Through Its Worst Heatwave on Record. Millions of Indians Live Right In It.
news.excerpt: Britain, France and Switzerland have all broken June temperature records as a 'killer' heatwave scientists link to climate change grips the continent. With dozens dead and code-red alerts from London to the Netherlands, the diaspora is feeling the heat too.
news.image_caption: A Copernicus Sentinel-3 satellite image of southern Europe during an exceptional heatwave. Western Europe is enduring its worst recorded heatwave, with the UK, France and Switzerland breaking June temperature records in late June 2026.
news.nri_angle: Europe's worst recorded heatwave is the weather outside the windows of millions of Indians who now call the continent home — roughly two million people of Indian origin in the UK alone, plus hundreds of thousands across France, Germany, Italy and the Netherlands — many living in homes built for a cool climate, without air conditioning, leaving elderly relatives, students in un-air-conditioned exam halls and outdoor workers acutely exposed as records fall and code-red alerts spread.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: 200 Indian Americans Just Walked Into 125 Congressional Offices in a Single Day
news.excerpt: The fourth annual FIIDS Capitol Hill Day on June 23 was the largest diaspora advocacy push yet — delegates from 25 states pressed lawmakers on US-India ties, high-skilled immigration and critical minerals, while Indian American Congressmen urged the community to stop watching from the sidelines and run for office.
news.image_caption: The United States Capitol. Nearly 200 Indian American delegates visited more than 125 Congressional offices during the fourth annual FIIDS Capitol Hill Day on June 23, 2026
news.nri_angle: The fourth annual FIIDS Capitol Hill Day on June 23, 2026 — nearly 200 Indian American delegates from 25 states working more than 125 Congressional offices in a single day — marks the diaspora's largest and most organised legislative advocacy push yet, pressing Washington on US-India ties, high-skilled immigration reform and critical minerals, while Indian American lawmakers urged the community to convert its economic weight into political power by running for office.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Australia's Under-16 Social Media Ban Isn't Working Yet — and Indian-Australian Families Have a Big Stake in What Happens Next
news.excerpt: Six months after the world-first ban took effect, a new study finds teen use is little changed, and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says he will toughen enforcement. With India now Australia's single largest source of migrants, the policy lands squarely on hundreds of thousands of diaspora households raising teenagers.
news.image_caption: Australia's world-first ban bars under-16s from holding accounts on major social media platforms. A new study finds teen use is little changed six months in
news.nri_angle: Six months after Australia's world-first ban on under-16 social media accounts, a new BMJ study finds teen use is little changed and PM Albanese is moving to toughen enforcement — a debate that lands directly on the diaspora, since India is now Australia's single largest source of migrants (971,020 India-born, up 55,000 in a year), meaning hundreds of thousands of Indian-Australian households raising teenagers have a direct stake in whether the law works and in the privacy trade-offs of stricter age checks.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Raised Passport Fees for the First Time in Years. Here's the New Price List.
news.excerpt: From July 1, a basic adult passport jumps from Rs 1,500 to Rs 2,500 and a lost-passport replacement under Tatkal can run to Rs 8,500. The Ministry of External Affairs has revised charges across every category, from minors to police clearance certificates.
news.image_caption: An Indian passport. The Ministry of External Affairs has raised passport fees across all categories effective July 1, 2026
news.nri_angle: India is raising passport fees across every category from July 1, 2026 — a basic adult passport rises to Rs 2,500 and a lost-passport Tatkal replacement to as much as Rs 8,500 — and because Indian missions abroad benchmark consular fees to the domestic schedule, NRIs renewing or replacing passports overseas should expect higher charges and can lock in the old rate by filing before July 1.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: You Can Now Clear Immigration in Varanasi and Fly to the World Through Delhi Without Touching Your Bags
news.excerpt: Air India's new 'Easy Connect' flights, launching from Varanasi on June 25, let travellers from smaller Indian cities check baggage through to their final destination and complete international immigration at their home airport. A phased rollout to more Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities is planned.
news.image_caption: An Air India aircraft. The airline's new 'Easy Connect' flights launch from Varanasi under the government's hub-and-spoke model
news.nri_angle: Air India's new 'Easy Connect' hub-and-spoke flights, launching from Varanasi on June 25 with a phased rollout to more Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, let travellers check baggage through to their final destination and clear international immigration at their home airport — a direct win for the large share of the diaspora whose roots are in smaller Indian cities and who have long endured collecting and re-checking bags and a second immigration queue at Delhi mid-journey.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Quietly Offering Its Diaspora a Rare Deal: Park Dollars Home, Earn Almost Like Stocks
news.excerpt: The RBI is swallowing the currency-hedging cost on new FCNR(B) deposits, pushing rates to 6-7%. With loans now allowed against those deposits through GIFT City, returns could climb toward double digits — and analysts expect tens of billions of NRI dollars to follow.
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, which is absorbing the hedging cost on new FCNR(B) diaspora deposits
news.nri_angle: The RBI is absorbing the currency-hedging cost on new three-to-five-year FCNR(B) deposits, pushing dollar rates for non-resident Indians to 6-7% with no rupee risk — and with loans now permitted against those deposits through GIFT City, leveraged returns could approach 12-15%, making 'sending money home' a genuinely competitive investment for the world's 35-million-strong Indian diaspora rather than an act of sentiment.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's UAE Embassy Is Hitting Pause on Passports and Visas for Five Days. Here's What 4 Million Indians Need to Know.
news.excerpt: Regular consular services in the UAE shut from June 26 to June 30 as the mission swaps outsourcing partners. From July 1, a new operator, Al Hind Tours and Travel, takes over passport, visa and attestation work.
news.image_caption: The Abu Dhabi skyline; the Indian Embassy is pausing regular passport, visa and consular services across the UAE from June 26 to 30 during a provider switch
news.nri_angle: Regular Indian passport, visa, attestation and consular services across the UAE — home to the world's largest Indian diaspora community of about 4.4 million — are paused from June 26 to 30 as the embassy switches its outsourced provider from BLS/SGIVS to Al Hind Tours and Travel, meaning non-emergency applicants should file before June 26 or wait until July 1, while already-submitted applications and genuine emergencies remain covered.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Shafali Verma Lights Up Old Trafford as India Keep Their World Cup Alive
news.excerpt: A 53 off 34 from the returning opener powered a five-wicket win over Bangladesh in Manchester. Now a Sunday showdown with Australia at Lord's will decide India's semifinal fate.
news.image_caption: Old Trafford in Manchester, where India beat Bangladesh by five wickets to keep their T20 World Cup campaign alive
news.nri_angle: The Women's T20 World Cup is being staged in England, home to roughly two million people of Indian origin, turning grounds like Old Trafford into diaspora gathering points; India's five-wicket win over Bangladesh and Shafali Verma's match-winning half-century keep the reigning ODI champions on course for a semifinal in front of their largest overseas fanbase, with a defining clash against Australia at Lord's on Sunday.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: 'If You Don't Have a Seat at the Table, You're on the Menu': The Diaspora's Loudest Year in Washington
news.excerpt: Nearly 200 Indian-American delegates fanned out across Capitol Hill this week as lawmakers urged the community to run for office — a civic surge sharpened by rising anti-Hindu and anti-India hate.
news.image_caption: The US Capitol, where nearly 200 Indian-American delegates lobbied more than 125 Congressional offices this week
news.nri_angle: The Indian-American community's largest-ever Capitol Hill advocacy day — 200 delegates pressing immigration reform and the green-card backlog — paired with lawmakers urging the diaspora to run for office amid rising anti-Hindu and anti-India hate, marks a strategic shift for NRIs from quiet professional success toward direct political representation, with the visa and PR backlog issues that affect millions of Indian families at the centre of the agenda.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Canada Issued Millions of Work Permits. Now They're Expiring — and Indians Are Half the Wave.
news.excerpt: About 1.4 million permits lapse in Canada this year against just 380,000 permanent-residency slots. The arithmetic doesn't work, and the people it strands are disproportionately Indian.
news.image_caption: An Air Canada aircraft at the gate. Tens of thousands of Indian work-permit holders face expiry in 2026 amid a permanent-residency backlog.
news.nri_angle: Indians make up roughly half of Canada's temporary-resident approvals, so the 2026 expiry wave — 1.4 million permits lapsing against just 380,000 PR slots — puts a uniquely large share of Indian students, workers and their spouses at risk of falling out of status or being forced to leave, with knock-on effects for remittances and a talent influx back into India.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: AI's Hunger for Memory Just Made Your Next Phone More Expensive. India Will Feel It Hardest.
news.excerpt: Memory-chip prices have leapt as much as 89% in a single quarter as AI data centres swallow the supply. Apple is already raising prices — and the world's second-biggest phone market is squarely in the blast radius.
news.image_caption: Memory modules like these have surged in price as AI data centres absorb global chip supply
news.nri_angle: India is the world's second-largest smartphone market and overwhelmingly price-sensitive, so the AI-driven 'RAMageddon' memory surge — already forcing Apple and rivals to raise prices — will hit Indian buyers of budget phones and laptops hard, even as Micron's new Sanand plant in Gujarat marks India's bet to climb the semiconductor ladder; NRIs face the same hikes abroad and a longer-term investment story in memory's shift from commodity to strategic asset.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Has Run Short of a Cancer Drug. It Just Sent an SOS to India's Drugmakers.
news.excerpt: The US FDA has quietly asked Indian manufacturers to supply ifosfamide — a chemotherapy in short supply after a US plant disruption — a reminder of how much the world's medicine cabinet leans on India.
news.image_caption: Vials of chemotherapy drugs; the US FDA has asked Indian manufacturers to help supply the cancer drug ifosfamide
news.nri_angle: An NRI family with a relative in cancer treatment in the US has a direct stake in whether ifosfamide stays on the shelf — and an Indian-made vial may be what fills the gap; the FDA's explicit appeal to Indian drugmakers underscores India's standing as the pharmacy of the world and offers the diaspora both reassurance and a recurring investment angle in names like Cipla, Alkem and Zydus.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Judge Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. Two Weeks Later, It's Quietly Back.
news.excerpt: A Boston court struck down the fee on June 8 as an unlawful tax — then paused its own ruling. USCIS may keep collecting the six-figure charge while the appeal proceeds, and Indians, the largest H-1B group, are again left guessing.
news.image_caption: A US visa in a passport; a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions is back in effect while a federal appeal proceeds
news.nri_angle: Indians receive the largest share of H-1B visas, so the on-again, off-again fate of Trump's $100,000 fee — struck down on June 8 but back in force days later while the First Circuit weighs the government's appeal — directly governs whether Indian engineers, doctors and researchers can still realistically be sponsored, and the resulting uncertainty is pushing many toward Canada or a return to India.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: U.N. Halts Strait of Hormuz Evacuation After Cargo Ship Is Attacked, Stranding Thousands of Sailors Again
news.excerpt: A drone strike on a tanker off Oman forces the IMO to suspend a rescue that had just freed 1,100 seafarers, reviving fears for the fragile U.S.-Iran deal and the Indians who crew the world's ships.
news.image_caption: A tanker lies at anchor waiting to enter port. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had begun to recover before Thursday's attack forced the U.N. to pause its evacuation.
news.nri_angle: India is the world's largest supplier of merchant seafarers, with some 18,000 Indians caught on ships in the Gulf and three already killed; a renewed Hormuz crisis also raises India's oil-import bill and pump prices felt across diaspora families.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Will Soon Let You Pay $750 to Skip the Visa Line. India's Travellers Are the Obvious Customer.
news.excerpt: A six-month State Department pilot starting July 1 lets visitor-visa applicants buy an interview within 10 business days — a paid fast lane in a system where Indians have long waited months for a slot.
news.image_caption: The U.S. Embassy in New Delhi; a new State Department pilot offers Indian travellers faster visa interviews for a fee
news.nri_angle: Indians generate some of the world's heaviest demand for US visitor visas and have long faced months-long appointment backlogs, so a paid fast lane offering an interview within 10 business days — for USD 750 on top of the USD 185 fee — lands squarely on the diaspora's frequent fliers, from parents visiting grandchildren to founders and professionals shuttling across the India-US corridor.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: After a Decade of Waiting, India's Biggest Stock Exchange Is Finally Going Public. The Owner of the Market Is About to Join It.
news.excerpt: The National Stock Exchange has filed for a roughly Rs 30,000-crore offer-for-sale — set to be India's largest-ever IPO — at a valuation near $55 billion, ending a listing saga that has dragged since 2016.
news.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange building in Mumbai; NSE has filed for what would be India's largest-ever IPO
news.nri_angle: NRIs increasingly route remittances and savings into Indian equities and index funds, and the NSE IPO offers a chance to own a piece of the marketplace itself — a stock that has been off-limits until now — with eligible NRIs able to apply via NRE/NRO portfolio accounts, while the back-to-back NSE and Jio mega-listings signal the deepening of the very markets the diaspora uses to keep financial roots at home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Adani Is Betting $2 Billion That the Next City Grows Around the Airport, Not the Other Way Around
news.excerpt: The group's airports arm will build 'airport cities' — hotels, offices, retail and entertainment — across more than 655 acres at six Indian airports, modelled on Singapore, Dubai and Amsterdam.
news.image_caption: An airport terminal in India; Adani Airports plans 'airport cities' across six Indian airports
news.nri_angle: NRIs experience India most often through its airports, and Adani's $2 billion bet on 'airport cities' at Mumbai, Ahmedabad and four other hubs means more hotels, business space and world-class terminals for diaspora travellers — while reshaping the earnings of a group that is a fixture of NRI investment portfolios directly and through Indian index funds.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: America's Oldest Indian Association Just Honoured Seven of Its Own. Four Were Doctors.
nri-world.excerpt: The AIA-NY benefit gala in Flushing celebrated a community's elite — and quietly revealed how narrow the diaspora's definition of success still is, even as a new generation pushes at the edges.
nri-world.image_caption: A Bharatanatyam dancer performs a classical Indian dance on stage, the kind of cultural showcase that anchors diaspora community galas.
nri-world.nri_angle: The honours list of the oldest national Indian-American association is a ritual of self-definition for a community built on professional-visa migration — and a window into whether its founding-era institutions can hold the loyalty of a startup-minded next generation.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Australia Just Honoured Ten Indian-Origin Citizens. None of Them Are Famous.
nri-world.excerpt: The 2026 King's Birthday Honours List reads like a map of how a migrant community embeds itself — through doctors, psychiatrists and the half-century grind of building institutions nobody else would.
nri-world.image_caption: Sydney's skyline, including the Opera House. Indians are now Australia's second-largest migrant community.
nri-world.nri_angle: Honours conferred by the Australian state — not by an Indian-community body — are a signal of belonging, recognising decades of professional and civic service by a migrant population that is now the country's second-largest.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Delhi Spent Years Wanting the Diaspora's Remittances. Now It Wants Its Portfolio.
nri-world.excerpt: A new RBI deposit scheme and the rise of GIFT City are reframing overseas Indians from senders of money home into investors in India — on terms built to compete with Dubai and New York.
nri-world.image_caption: Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City), India's tax-neutral financial hub courting NRI capital
nri-world.nri_angle: Overseas Indians are being courted with hedged, leveraged double-digit returns and tax-efficient GIFT City products that let them treat India as a serious portfolio allocation rather than just a place to send remittances.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Forbes Named America's 250 Most Successful Immigrants. Twenty-Six Are Indian.
nri-world.excerpt: Timed to the US's 250th anniversary, the list reads like a diaspora scoreboard — and quietly maps both how far Indian-Americans have climbed and where they still haven't.
nri-world.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, one of 26 Indian-origin leaders on the inaugural Forbes 250 immigrants list
nri-world.nri_angle: The Forbes immigrant list is a measure of how thoroughly the Indian diaspora has woven itself into the top of the American economy — and an instruction, for a community fond of measuring itself, on the boardrooms and offices it still hasn't cracked.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Quiet Clause in the India-UK Trade Deal That Puts Money Back in Diaspora Payslips
nri-world.excerpt: From 15 July, a Double Contribution Convention ends the double social-security charge on Indian professionals posted to Britain — the human core of a deal usually sold on tariffs.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, in London for talks ahead of the India-UK trade pact rollout
nri-world.nri_angle: For the thousands of Indian professionals rotated through British client sites, the Double Contribution Convention ends years of paying into a UK pension they would never collect — a small, specific win for the diaspora inside a sweeping trade pact.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora's Money Is Pouring Home at Record Levels. It's Also Quietly Changing Shape.
nri-world.excerpt: India will take in nearly $140 billion in remittances this year. The bigger story is the shift from Gulf wages to Western capital — and how Delhi is racing to court it.
nri-world.nri_angle: For 18.5 million Indians abroad, sending money home is shifting from obligation to investment — and India is now pricing the bond with competitive interest rates, equity caps and property rule changes aimed squarely at the diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A 23-Year-Old and His Mother Just Became Mayors a Week Apart. Both Still Teach Hindi on Weekends.
nri-world.excerpt: Tushar Kumar and Parveen Rani's back-to-back Hertfordshire mayoralties are a feel-good headline — and a window into how the diaspora's British political climb now runs through the council chamber.
nri-world.image_caption: A civic building in London, where Indian-origin councillors are steadily taking on mayoral and council roles
nri-world.nri_angle: Britain's 1.9-million-strong Indian community is building political power from the ground up — in town halls and civic chains — and the Kumar-Rani story captures the second-generation balancing act of staying rooted while serving a chosen country.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Every Summer, 10,000 Telugu-Americans Fill a Convention Center. It's Not Really About the Concert.
nri-world.excerpt: From TANA in Dallas to ATA in Baltimore, the diaspora's convention circuit has become the load-bearing infrastructure of a community trying to keep its language alive one generation at a time.
nri-world.image_caption: A Bharatanatyam dancer in traditional attire, the kind of classical performance that anchors diaspora cultural conventions
nri-world.nri_angle: The biennial Telugu conventions are an organised answer to the second-generation problem every immigrant community faces — how to pass on a language and culture that the home country can no longer enforce from 12,000 km away.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Has Quietly Rewritten the Rulebook for Its 4.5 Million OCI Holders. Here's What Changed.
nri-world.excerpt: A new digital e-OCI system, a USD 275 fee for fresh cards, a hard three-month deadline to update your record after a new passport, and the death of the old PIO card add up to the biggest shake-up of the scheme in years.
nri-world.image_caption: An Indian passport; India has overhauled the rules tying OCI cards to a holder's current passport
nri-world.nri_angle: The OCI card is the document that keeps roughly 4.5 million people of Indian origin connected to India — visa-free entry and the right to live and work there — and the 2026 overhaul raises fees, kills the old PIO card, and imposes a hard three-month deadline (with a penalty) to update the record after every new passport, hitting frequent flyers, overseas students and mixed-passport families hardest.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Forty-One Years On, the Diaspora Still Gathers for Air India 182. The State Mostly Doesn't.
nri-world.excerpt: On June 23, families lit candles from Stanley Park to Ahakista for the 329 people killed in the world's deadliest act of aviation terrorism before 9/11 — a grief that built Canada's South Asian community and a justice it never received.
nri-world.image_caption: The Air India Flight 182 memorial at Humber Bay Park East in Etobicoke, Toronto
nri-world.nri_angle: The 1985 Air India bombing killed 268 Canadians, most of them of Indian origin, and remains the deadliest terror attack in Canadian history — a foundational wound for the Indo-Canadian community, whose families have spent four decades organizing memorials and fighting the perception that their dead were treated as a foreign tragedy rather than a Canadian one.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian-Australians Give Generously. A New Study Wants to Know Why So Little of It Is Counted.
nri-world.excerpt: Now the largest overseas-born group in Australia, the community gives out of faith, family and duty — but mostly outside the formal channels that track, deduct and amplify philanthropy. Researchers think that is a missed opportunity worth measuring.
nri-world.image_caption: Performers play traditional drums at an Indian community cultural festival
nri-world.nri_angle: Indians are now the largest overseas-born community in Australia, yet their considerable charitable giving is largely invisible to the formal philanthropic sector because it flows through temples, family networks and remittances home rather than registered foundations — a gap a new research effort aims to map, with implications for how the diaspora's wealth shapes both Australian causes and India.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Europe Is Quietly Courting Indian Students — and Seeding the Diaspora's Next Chapter
nri-world.excerpt: The EU has awarded 75 Indians Erasmus Mundus scholarships and launched a student ambassadors' network, building the connective tissue that turns student flows into settled communities.
nri-world.image_caption: International students at a European university (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: Where students go is where communities eventually form. Europe's deliberate recruitment of Indian talent is the early signature of diaspora clusters that do not yet fully exist — as old America-or-Britain defaults loosen.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Meta Bets $900 Million on an Indian Fintech — and Hands an Indian Founder the Keys to WhatsApp
markets-finance.excerpt: Meta is investing about $900 million in Bengaluru-based CRED at a $4.5 billion valuation and has named its founder, Kunal Shah, the global head of WhatsApp — a twin move that signals how central India has become to the messaging giant's push into payments.
markets-finance.image_caption: CRED founder Kunal Shah, named global head of WhatsApp as Meta invests about $900 million in his fintech (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: WhatsApp is the default communication tool binding the Indian diaspora to family back home, and the elevation of an Indian fintech founder with no Silicon Valley pedigree to run it — alongside a near-billion-dollar bet on an Indian startup — is both a marker of diaspora ascent in Big Tech leadership and a sign that the payments and commerce features NRIs use to send money and shop across borders are about to be reimagined from an Indian playbook.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Biggest Stock Exchange Files to Go Public — in What Would Be the Country's Largest IPO Ever
markets-finance.excerpt: After nearly a decade of regulatory delay, the National Stock Exchange has filed for a roughly Rs 30,000-crore listing valuing it near Rs 5 lakh crore. But it is a pure offer for sale — every rupee goes to existing owners cashing out, not into the company.
markets-finance.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange has filed for what would be India's largest-ever initial public offering (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: The NSE is the venue where almost every Indian equity an NRI owns is traded, and a listing of the exchange itself — India's largest-ever IPO — is a marquee, heavily oversubscribed event diaspora investors will want a piece of, even as its structure as a pure cash-out by existing owners is a warning worth heeding before they chase the grey-market hype.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India and America Say a Trade Deal Is 'Very Close' — but It Hinges on One Word: Advantage
markets-finance.excerpt: New Delhi insists it will not let the long-awaited pact take effect unless Washington guarantees India a tariff edge over rivals like Vietnam and Bangladesh, with a July deadline now concentrating minds on both sides.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's commerce minister Piyush Goyal, who said the India-US trade deal is finalised but awaits a tariff-advantage guarantee
markets-finance.nri_angle: A US-India trade pact would reshape the cost of everything from Indian pharmaceuticals and textiles to the cross-border businesses many NRIs run or invest in — and as the largest single bridge between the two economies the diaspora straddles, its terms touch their portfolios, their companies and the broader India growth story they are betting on.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: America Runs Short of a Cancer Drug — and Sends an SOS to India's Generic Makers
markets-finance.excerpt: With the chemotherapy drug ifosfamide in short supply, the US FDA has quietly asked Indian manufacturers to step in. The episode lifted pharma stocks and underscored, once again, the world's reliance on India's drug industry.
markets-finance.image_caption: The US FDA has asked Indian generic drugmakers to help supply the cancer drug ifosfamide amid a US shortage
markets-finance.nri_angle: It is a vivid reminder of how central India is to the medicines the diaspora and the wider world depend on — the same Indian generic makers being asked to rescue a US cancer-drug shortage are core holdings in many NRI portfolios, and the episode sits at the centre of the simmering India-US trade conversation.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Turns to Its Diaspora to Steady the Rupee — and Dangles an Unusually Sweet Deposit Deal
markets-finance.excerpt: By absorbing the cost of hedging, the Reserve Bank of India has let banks raise dollar-deposit rates to 6-7% for overseas Indians, with leverage potentially pushing returns far higher. Analysts see tens of billions in inflows.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India is absorbing hedging costs to draw diaspora dollar deposits and support the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: This is a scheme built expressly for the diaspora: it lets overseas Indians earn elevated, currency-risk-free returns on dollar deposits in Indian banks, turning the community's savings into both a personal opportunity and a national lifeline for the rupee — the most directly NRI-targeted financial move of the year.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Quietly Sells Down Its Crown Jewels — the IRFC Stake Sale Shows the Disinvestment Machine Is Back
markets-finance.excerpt: The government offloaded up to 2% of Indian Railway Finance Corporation at a discount, and institutions snapped it up. It is the latest in a string of stake sales as New Delhi leans on its state-owned giants to plug the budget.
markets-finance.image_caption: An Indian Railways train; the government sold up to 2% of Indian Railway Finance Corporation
markets-finance.nri_angle: These offer-for-sale windows in marquee state-owned companies are some of the most accessible entry points for NRIs to buy into India’s infrastructure and banking story, often at a built-in discount — so the return of an active disinvestment calendar directly shapes where diaspora investors can put their money to work back home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Market Engine Has Quietly Switched Drivers — From Foreign Money to the Monthly SIP
markets-finance.excerpt: Even as foreign investors pulled roughly $36 billion out of Indian equities and the Nifty went almost nowhere for two years, ordinary savers kept feeding the market through automated monthly plans — a shift JP Morgan calls the country's new 'demand anchor.'
markets-finance.image_caption: Mumbai's financial district, where domestic monthly investment plans have become the dominant force in Indian equities
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs weighing whether to keep money in Indian equities should understand that the market is now propped up less by the foreign flows they watch in the headlines and more by a domestic savings wave — a structural change that affects both the risks and the resilience of any India allocation.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Quietly Talking Itself Out of Gold — and the World's Bullion Market Is Feeling It
markets-finance.excerpt: Domestic gold has slid to its lowest price since early April, dealers are quoting steep discounts, and the country's gold ETFs just logged their first monthly outflow in a year. Behind the cooling is a deliberate push to curb gold buying and defend a battered rupee.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian gold demand has cooled to multi-month lows as the country curbs buying to defend the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: Gold is woven into diaspora life — the wedding jewellery, the festival purchases, the rupee-denominated savings that NRIs hold as a hedge — so India’s campaign to cool gold demand, the slide in domestic prices and the steep dealer discounts directly shape when and how non-resident Indians buy, gift and store the metal both abroad and back home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian Markets Roar Back as Oil Crashes and the Central Bank Calms Rate Fears
markets-finance.excerpt: A day after a brutal selloff, the Sensex jumped nearly 800 points and the Nifty reclaimed 24,000, powered by banks and IT, as Brent crude tumbled to four-month lows on signs the Strait of Hormuz was reopening and the RBI signalled no rate hike is coming.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Sensex rallied nearly 800 points on June 24 as oil prices fell and the RBI eased rate-hike fears
markets-finance.nri_angle: The same falling oil price and steadier rupee that lifted Mumbai’s indices directly shape what NRIs see — the value of remittances sent home, the returns on Indian equity and bond holdings, and the cost of the fuel and imports that drive India’s inflation — and a fresh RBI rule now lets banks lend to non-resident Indians against their foreign-currency deposits.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Threw Open Its Bond Market to the World. The World Is Still Deciding Whether to Walk In.
markets-finance.excerpt: After scrapping the tax on foreign holdings of government bonds and widening access, India has lured early buyers — including a rare $1 billion bet by Canada's Fairfax — and is angling for a coveted Bloomberg index seat. But a weak rupee and steep hedging costs may yet keep the big money cautious.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's bond-market reforms aim to lure global investors as a weak rupee tests their appetite
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's push to pull global money into its government bonds runs on the same engine the diaspora is being courted with — dollar deposits, GIFT City, index inclusion — and the outcome will shape the yields, the rupee and the investment options NRIs see when they decide how much of their savings to send home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Opens a New Door to the World's Markets — and It Runs Through GIFT City
markets-finance.excerpt: A wave of new funds is letting Indians invest in US stocks and global assets through the country's tax-neutral financial hub, with the fund itself shouldering the tax — but the fine print on remittance limits and levies still rewards a careful reading.
markets-finance.image_caption: An Indian financial-district skyline; new funds based in GIFT City are opening fresh routes for Indians and NRIs to invest in global markets
markets-finance.nri_angle: GIFT City is being built explicitly to court the diaspora's capital, and for NRIs weighing how to hold global assets with an Indian foot, the new IFSC funds change the calculus on tax, repatriation and paperwork — exactly the friction points that have long made cross-border investing a headache.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Jio Files for India's Biggest-Ever IPO — but This Time, the Marquee Backers Don't Get to Cash Out
markets-finance.excerpt: Reliance's digital arm has filed papers for a roughly $3.8 billion listing, with every rupee earmarked for debt and growth — meaning the Meta, Google and Gulf investors who poured in during 2020 will have to wait their turn.
markets-finance.image_caption: Reliance Jio's headquarters. Jio Platforms has filed a draft prospectus for what would be India's largest-ever IPO.
markets-finance.nri_angle: Jio's listing will be the marquee Indian IPO of a generation, and NRIs — long among the most eager retail buyers of marquee Indian names — will be weighing whether to chase it; the unusual all-fresh-issue structure and the holding-company discount are exactly the fine print diaspora investors need to read before committing.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Teenage Shooters Are Topping a World Championship in Germany — and Rewriting the Record Book
sports.excerpt: At the ISSF Junior World Championship in Suhl, India leads the medal table with five golds, while a 10m air rifle pair set a new junior world record — a preview of the talent pipeline aimed at Los Angeles 2028.
sports.image_caption: An Indian junior in the 10m air rifle final at a youth world shooting event, the same discipline in which India's teenagers topped the ISSF Junior World Championship in Suhl.
sports.image_credit: Martin Rulsch, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
sports.nri_angle: Shooting has quietly become India's most reliable Olympic medal factory, and the teenagers topping the ISSF Junior World Championship in Suhl — a junior world record included — are the names NRIs should learn now, because they are the ones aimed at the Los Angeles 2028 Games.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Down 0-4 to a Bullet Specialist, Arjun Erigaisi Won the Next 16 — and a Shot at the World's Fastest Chess Title
sports.excerpt: India's No. 1 thrashed two-time runner-up Andrew Tang 16-6 to reach the Bullet Chess Championship Winners Final, with Nihal Sarin still alive in the bracket — the clearest sign yet that India now owns the fastest format in the game.
sports.image_caption: Indian grandmaster Arjun Erigaisi, who beat Andrew Tang 16-6 to reach the Winners Final of the 2026 Bullet Chess Championship.
sports.nri_angle: Online speed chess is where the diaspora watches India's golden generation in real time — free global streams, results in minutes — and Arjun Erigaisi one win from a Grand Final in the world's fastest format, alongside Nihal Sarin, is exactly the bite-sized Indian triumph NRIs rally around and share.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: One Year After the Injury That Cost Her a Season, Jyothi Yarraji Is Back Under 13 Seconds
sports.excerpt: At the National Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar, India's first Olympic 100m hurdler ran 12.99 to win gold — the number she had been chasing since a knee injury wiped out much of her 2025.
sports.image_caption: The Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar, host of the 65th National Inter-State Senior Athletics Championships, where Jyothi Yarraji ran 12.99 to win the 100m hurdles.
sports.image_credit: Government of Odisha, via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
sports.nri_angle: For an Indian diaspora that has learned to follow Olympic track and field through Neeraj Chopra, Jyothi Yarraji is the next name to know — the first Indian woman to run the 100m hurdles at a Games — and her comeback from a season-ending injury, capped by a sub-13 run in Bhubaneswar, is exactly the arc NRI sports fans rally behind ahead of the Asian Games.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: An 18-Year-Old With an Indian Flag on His Helmet Is the Closest Thing F1 Has Had to India in 15 Years
sports.excerpt: Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad — born to a British-Indian mother and a Swedish father — arrives at this weekend's Austrian Grand Prix as the only driver of Indian heritage on the grid since Karun Chandhok in 2011.
sports.image_caption: Arvid Lindblad, the 18-year-old Racing Bulls rookie of Indian and Swedish heritage, in Melbourne during the 2026 Formula 1 season.
sports.nri_angle: Arvid Lindblad, born to a British-Indian mother, is the first driver of Indian heritage on the Formula 1 grid since Karun Chandhok in 2011 — giving the diaspora a reason to follow the sport again as he races this weekend in Austria.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Shuttlers Have Brought Their Season to California — and Opened the US Open With a Near-Clean Sweep
sports.excerpt: From veteran Kidambi Srikanth to 17-year-old Tanvi Sharma, India's badminton contingent swept through the first round of the US Open in Fullerton, a Super 300 event staged on the doorstep of one of America's largest South Asian communities.
sports.image_caption: Kidambi Srikanth in action; the former world No. 1 is the No. 5 seed in India's US Open contingent in Fullerton, California.
sports.nri_angle: A full-strength Indian badminton contingent is competing in a sanctioned BWF event on US soil in Fullerton, California, putting the country's shuttlers within driving distance of one of America's largest South Asian communities.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Big-League Cricket Has Moved Into the Oakland Coliseum — and the Bay Area's Team Lost the First Round
sports.excerpt: Major League Cricket's fourth season has turned the old A's ballpark into the home of the playoffs and the final, but the San Francisco Unicorns opened their Oakland stand with a 22-run defeat to the Texas Super Kings.
sports.image_caption: An aerial view of the Oakland Coliseum, which is hosting Major League Cricket matches, the playoffs and the 2026 final.
sports.nri_angle: Major League Cricket has brought top-flight T20 cricket — and its 2026 playoffs and final — to the Oakland Coliseum, putting international-calibre players within a short drive of the Bay Area's large South Asian diaspora.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Shafali Verma Drags India Out of the Danger Zone — and Into a Sunday Showdown With Australia
sports.excerpt: A 34-ball 53 anchored India's five-wicket chase of Bangladesh at Old Trafford, a must-win that keeps them second in a three-way logjam and sets up a final group decider against the unbeaten champions at Lord's.
sports.image_caption: Shafali Verma, whose 34-ball 53 anchored India's chase against Bangladesh at the Women's T20 World Cup.
sports.nri_angle: The Women's T20 World Cup is being played on English grounds, putting India's title defence within reach of diaspora fans across the UK — with Sunday's decisive group game against Australia at Lord's.

sports.title: A New Captain, and a 15-Year-Old Knocking: India Begin the Iyer Era in Belfast
sports.excerpt: Shreyas Iyer leads India for the first time in Friday's opening T20I against Ireland, and the toughest call of his debut is whether to break up a World Cup-winning top three to fit teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
sports.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer, who captains India in T20Is for the first time against Ireland in Belfast.
sports.nri_angle: The two-match series is played on diaspora doorsteps in the British Isles and offers NRIs a first look at India under new T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, plus the possible international debut of 15-year-old viral sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: One Centimetre, and the Record Is His Alone: Dev Meena Vaults to 5.46m
sports.excerpt: The 21-year-old from Madhya Pradesh cleared 5.46m at the National Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar, breaking the men's pole vault national record he had shared with his training partner and booking his ticket to the Asian Games.
sports.image_caption: Indian pole vaulter Dev Meena, who broke the men's national record with a clearance of 5.46m.
sports.nri_angle: Pole vault has rarely featured in NRI sports conversations, but Dev Meena's record run and dual Asian Games and Commonwealth Games qualification give diaspora fans a new Indian track-and-field name to follow as both Games approach.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Women Won a Trophy and a Promotion in One Night in Auckland
sports.excerpt: Two first-quarter penalty corners beat hosts New Zealand 2-0 in the FIH Hockey Women's Nations Cup final, handing Salima Tete's unbeaten side the title and a direct return to the elite Pro League barely a year after relegation.
sports.image_caption: India captain Salima Tete, who led the team to an unbeaten FIH Hockey Women's Nations Cup title in Auckland.
sports.nri_angle: India's women returning to the FIH Pro League means diaspora fans across Europe and beyond will get far more chances to watch the national team play live next season, as Pro League fixtures tour host cities worldwide.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Have Never Won at Edgbaston. Now They Must — and Decide Whether to Risk Bumrah to Do It
sports.excerpt: Trailing England 0-1, Shubman Gill's young side arrives in Birmingham for the second Test on July 2 facing a green pitch, a venue that has beaten India eight times out of eight, and the recurring question of whether to spend their best bowler now or save him for Lord's.
sports.image_caption: India pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, whose availability for the Edgbaston Test is the central selection question of the tour.
sports.nri_angle: Edgbaston sits in the heart of Britain's largest South Asian community, making the second Test the closest thing to a home game for UK-based Indian fans — a rare in-person chance to watch Shubman Gill's new-look side try to level the series and finally win at the one English ground that has always beaten India.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's 15-Year-Old Prodigy Will Change in a Room of His Own — the Safeguarding Rule Behind It
sports.excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi can sit in India's dressing room during play and join every team talk, but ICC and English safeguarding rules bar an under-16 from changing alongside adults — so on the tours of Ireland and England, his parents come too.
sports.image_caption: India's 15-year-old batting prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, named in the T20I squad for the tours of Ireland and England.
sports.nri_angle: Britain and Ireland's Indian community gets a rare home-soil look at India's 15-year-old prodigy this summer, and the UK safeguarding rules forcing a separate dressing room show how child-protection norms apply even to touring stars — with a potential record-breaking debut on local grounds.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI Built Its Own AI Chip and Called It Jalapeño. The Real Target Is Nvidia's Fattest Margin.
technology.excerpt: Designed with Broadcom and fabbed at TSMC, the inference chip promises 50% cheaper compute — and a quiet escape from the GPU that made every Indian AI engineer's resume valuable.
technology.image_caption: A semiconductor wafer under magnification, the kind of inference silicon now being custom-designed by AI labs.
technology.nri_angle: Indian engineers staff the inference, infra, and silicon teams at OpenAI, Broadcom, and TSMC's US operations — and a shift from buying Nvidia GPUs to designing custom chips reshapes which skills get hired and which get commoditized.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Wipro Just Posted $10.5 Billion in Revenue and Spun Up an 'AI-Native' Unit. The Subtext Is About Who It Stops Hiring.
technology.excerpt: Stable margins, a new forward-deployed engineering arm, and small language models for clients — Wipro's FY26 results map the exact direction India's IT giants are pulling the diaspora's careers.
technology.image_caption: A gate entrance at Wipro's Electronic City campus in Bengaluru.
technology.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers — many on H-1B and L-1 visas at Wipro's US client sites — are watching whether 'AI-native' delivery means a promotion path or a pink slip as the services model gets rebuilt around agents.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's IT Titans Lost ₹8.5 Lakh Crore in Five Years. The Money Walked Into AI Startups That Didn't Exist Then.
technology.excerpt: A new Hurun ranking shows TCS, Infosys, and Wipro as the only major sector to shed value, while pure-play AI names like Sarvam climb the charts — a wealth migration NRI investors can't afford to misread.
technology.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India's oldest equity market.
technology.nri_angle: NRIs allocating to India through IT-heavy index funds and ADRs may be over-indexed on yesterday's winners; the value shift toward homegrown AI signals where the next decade of returns — and return-to-India bets — may actually sit.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Meta Just Made a CRED Founder the Boss of WhatsApp. The Real Prize Is the 500 Million Indians Who Already Live There.
technology.excerpt: Kunal Shah, who built CRED into India's slickest fintech, takes over the world's biggest messaging app alongside Meta's $900 million bet on his company. The job is to finally make WhatsApp pay — and India is the test lab.
technology.image_caption: CRED founder Kunal Shah, named global head of WhatsApp. The real prize is the 500 million Indians already on the app (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Most NRIs run their entire Indian lives through WhatsApp — family groups, the neighbourhood kirana, airline alerts — so a payments-and-commerce overhaul led by a founder who understands Indian consumer behaviour will reshape how the diaspora moves money and shops across borders.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Hackers Dumped 630GB From the Factory That Builds a Third of India's iPhones. Apple and Tesla's Secrets Were Inside.
technology.excerpt: Tata Electronics confirmed a ransomware breach after the group World Leaks posted more than 200,000 stolen files — including documents marked as Apple and Tesla trade secrets — on the dark web.
technology.image_caption: An iPhone assembly line run by Tata Electronics in India. Hackers leaked 630GB from a plant that builds a third of India's iPhones (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: India's pitch to the diaspora and the world is that it can be a trusted alternative to China for building Apple iPhones and Tesla parts — and a 630GB leak of client trade secrets from Tata's flagship plant strikes directly at that promise, with the careers and reputations of Indian engineers riding on it.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's First Big Chip Plant Promises 48 Million Units Out of Assam by November. The Map Just Moved East.
technology.excerpt: Tata Semiconductor's packaging facility in Guwahati is on track to begin exports this year, a tangible milestone for the India Semiconductor Mission as TSMC publicly backs the country's ambitions at a Bengaluru summit.
technology.image_caption: Inside a semiconductor fabrication plant. India's first big chip facility in Assam promises 48 million units by November (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin semiconductor professionals across the Bay Area and Austin have spent years asking whether India's chip mission would ever ship a real product — and the first commercial output from an Assam plant turns a slogan into a supply chain they may one day return to or invest in.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Akash Ambani Wants to Put 1,600 Satellites Over India. He's Picking a Fight With Starlink in Orbit.
technology.excerpt: At the Reliance AGM, Jio unveiled plans for a homegrown low-earth-orbit constellation and a $10-15 billion bet to keep India's broadband sovereign. For NRIs, it is a wager on who controls the sky over the homeland.
technology.image_caption: A train of Starlink satellites photographed in low-earth orbit from a Chilean observatory
technology.nri_angle: The race to wire India from orbit decides whether the diaspora's family villages get fast broadband from an Indian operator or a foreign one, and whether a future Jio satellite IPO becomes the next big NRI investment story.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Satya Nadella's Xbox Just Got $150 Pricier and Game Pass Jumped 50%. Blame the Same Chip Crunch Hitting Everyone.
technology.excerpt: Microsoft hiked console and subscription prices overnight, citing memory costs set to double again by 2027. For the diaspora's large gaming community, the cost of play is now an AI-economy story.
technology.image_caption: The Xbox Series X and the smaller Series S console, both hit by Microsoft's price increases
technology.nri_angle: Xbox and Game Pass are staples in Indian American households where gaming bridges generations and continents, so a steep US price hike reshapes family budgets — even as the squeeze enriches the Indian-led memory supplier on the other side of the trade.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI May Wait Until 2027 to Go Public — Because Sam Altman Wants a $1 Trillion Price Tag.
technology.excerpt: A reported IPO delay sent AI stocks reeling from Seoul to New York, tripping a KOSPI circuit breaker. For the diaspora's army of AI engineers and investors, the timing of the decade's biggest listing just got murkier.
technology.image_caption: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, whose IPO timing is rattling global AI markets
technology.nri_angle: Indians fill the research benches at OpenAI and its rivals and tilt their portfolios toward the AI trade, so when the sector's defining IPO slips and a global selloff follows, both diaspora careers and diaspora savings feel the tremor.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nikesh Arora Held 800 Sales Meetings in 12 Weeks. The AI Cyberthreat He's Selling Against Is Bigger Than His Stock.
technology.excerpt: Palo Alto Networks just posted 31% revenue growth and record demand as enterprises scramble to defend AI systems. For the diaspora's huge security workforce, it is the rare tech segment still hiring into the AI wave.
technology.image_caption: Palo Alto Networks chairman and CEO Nikesh Arora speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt
technology.nri_angle: Cybersecurity is the rare corner of US tech still expanding headcount through the AI shakeout, and it sits under one of the highest-paid Indian-origin CEOs in the Valley — a real signal for diaspora engineers weighing where their skills stay durable.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Apple Just Raised MacBook Prices and Blamed a Memory Shortage. The Diaspora's Next India Trip Just Got More Useful.
technology.excerpt: A chip-memory squeeze dubbed 'RAMageddon' pushed Apple to lift iPad and Mac prices for the first time mid-cycle, wiping $250 billion off its value. The same crunch is minting record profits at Indian-led Micron.
technology.image_caption: Apple raised MacBook prices, citing a memory shortage (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Higher US device prices change the household math for NRIs who already shuttle gadgets between India and America, while the memory shortage driving them is fattening the profits of Indian-led Micron and its planned Gujarat fab.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Just Processed 23 Billion Digital Payments in a Single Month. The Number Should Worry Visa and Mastercard.
technology.excerpt: UPI handled Rs 29.9 lakh crore in May alone, up nearly 19% in a year, as PhonePe holds 46% of the market. For NRIs, the rails they use to send money home are quietly becoming a global export.
technology.image_caption: India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processed 23 billion transactions in a single month (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: UPI is the plumbing NRIs increasingly use to pay, split bills and send money across the India-US corridor, and its international push means the diaspora may soon scan the same QR codes abroad that they use back home.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Five Minutes Every Hour: A Simple Movement Habit Lifted Mood and Cut Fatigue, a Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Short walking breaks scattered through the workday eased fatigue and brightened mood in nearly 11,500 adults — and, contrary to the fear that stepping away hurts output, work performance edged up rather than down, researchers report.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: People out for a brisk walk. A new study finds five-minute movement breaks each hour lift mood and cut fatigue (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: A large share of the Indian diaspora works in desk-bound technology, finance and professional jobs where ten-hour sitting days are routine, layered on a genetic predisposition to early heart disease and diabetes — so a study showing that five-minute walking breaks an hour, with no gym and no lost productivity, can lift mood and break up dangerous sitting offers NRI knowledge workers a free, frictionless lever for both mind and metabolism.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It May Not Be How Much Protein You Eat, but One Amino Acid — a New Longevity-Diet Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A mostly plant-and-fish diet, kept low in protein but topped up with a small, sufficient amount of methionine — the amino acid in eggs, meat and dairy — extended healthy lifespan and cut frailty and fat in a USC study, challenging the idea that cutting calories is the key to staying lean.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A plant-and-fish Mediterranean-style diet, kept low in protein, was at the heart of the USC longevity study
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Many Indian-origin households already eat a largely vegetarian, plant-forward diet — exactly the base this 'longevity diet' is built on — yet the same group faces high rates of frailty, sarcopenia and early diabetes, so a study showing that a touch of the right protein (a little fish, egg or dairy for methionine) rather than more protein or fewer calories is what protects muscle and lifespan speaks directly to how NRI families can fine-tune a diet they mostly follow already.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It May Not Be How Many Fruits You Eat, but Which Ones — a 30,000-Person Study Points to the Heart
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Fewer than one in five people get enough flavanols, the heart-friendly compounds concentrated in apples with their skin, berries, plums, broad beans and green tea — even among those who dutifully hit their five-a-day, an international study using blood and urine markers finds.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Berries, apples with their skins and green tea are among the foods richest in heart-friendly flavanols
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian diaspora kitchens lean heavily on mangoes, bananas and citrus while the quietly flavanol-rich foods — apples eaten with the skin, berries, plums, broad beans and green tea — often sit at the edges of the plate, so a study showing it is the specific foods, not just the serving count, that protect the heart gives health-conscious NRI families a precise, low-cost lever against a community already prone to early cardiovascular disease.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Weight-Loss Pill, Taken Any Time of Day, Shed Up to 12% in a Year in an Early Trial
lifestyle-health.excerpt: An experimental oral GLP-1 drug, aleniglipron, helped overweight and obese adults lose as much as 12 percent of their body weight over 36 weeks with few side effects — and, unusually, can be swallowed at any time without the strict fasting rules of existing pills.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An experimental oral GLP-1 pill helped adults lose up to 12 percent of body weight in an early trial
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Obesity and type 2 diabetes strike the Indian diaspora earlier and at lower body weights than many other groups, yet injectable weight-loss drugs are costly and off-putting — so a cheap-to-make oral GLP-1 that works without injections or rigid fasting rules could matter enormously for NRI families, especially as India's generic industry stands ready to mass-produce such pills.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The 'Sunshine Vitamin' Many Are Missing — Even in Summer, and Most of All Those With Darker Skin
lifestyle-health.excerpt: New research finds large numbers of people run low on vitamin D year-round without knowing it — nearly three in four with darker skin pigmentation in one study — just as a separate trial suggests that getting levels right can sharply cut heart-attack risk.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: New research finds vitamin D deficiency is common year-round, especially among people with darker skin pigmentation
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Vitamin D is made in the skin from sunlight, and darker skin makes far less of it — so Indian-origin families living in the cloudier, higher-latitude cities of the US, UK and Canada are among the most likely in the world to be quietly deficient, a risk that compounds the community's existing vulnerability to diabetes and heart disease.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: For Those With Alzheimer's in the Family, One Eating Pattern Stood Out, a New Analysis Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Among people genetically predisposed to Alzheimer's, researchers found that an anti-inflammatory diet — not a Mediterranean or a generally 'healthy' one — was the only pattern tied to a meaningfully lower risk, pointing to inflammation as a lever the high-risk can pull.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An anti-inflammatory diet rich in leafy greens, berries and legumes was tied to lower Alzheimer's risk in the genetically predisposed
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Alzheimer's and dementia run in many Indian families, and the community already carries a high genetic and metabolic risk — so a finding that the predisposed may benefit most from a specifically anti-inflammatory diet, one that maps neatly onto traditional Indian staples like lentils, leafy greens, turmeric and vegetables, offers an actionable lever rather than a fatalistic shrug.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Single Habit — Regular Exercise — May Head Off Nearly Half of Dementia Cases, Researchers Say
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Of the fourteen lifestyle and environmental factors that shape dementia risk, six can be tackled through exercise alone, University of Minnesota researchers report — and a virtual program shows even rural adults far from gyms can do it from home.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Researchers say regular exercise can address six of the fourteen modifiable risk factors for dementia
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry an elevated, earlier risk of both diabetes and dementia, and aging diaspora parents are often scattered far from family and specialist care — so a finding that one accessible, no-cost habit, deliverable even by telehealth at home, can address six of dementia's biggest risk factors is unusually relevant to Indian-origin households.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Three Everyday Sleep Habits May Be Quietly Aging the Brain, a 23,000-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Sleeping outside the recommended seven-to-nine-hour window, napping often during the day and struggling with sleeplessness were each linked to more of the brain damage that builds up with age — and all three, researchers note, can be changed.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of 23,000 middle-aged and older adults links three common sleep habits to brain aging
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian-origin professionals abroad routinely run on short, broken sleep — late video calls with family in India, demanding jobs across time zones, the cultural habit of the afternoon nap — so evidence that these specific patterns may accelerate brain aging hands the diaspora a concrete, no-cost lever to protect long-term cognitive health.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Even 'Safe' Air May Be Hardening the Heart's Arteries, a Large Imaging Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Scanning the hearts of more than 11,000 adults, researchers found that long-term exposure to air pollution — even at levels below regulatory limits — was tied to more advanced coronary artery disease, with women facing a markedly higher risk.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A large imaging study tied long-term air pollution, even at safe levels, to more advanced coronary artery disease
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian-origin families straddle two air-quality worlds — long stays in some of the planet's most polluted cities back home and daily life in Western suburbs assumed to be clean — so a finding that even 'safe' air damages arteries reframes pollution as a heart risk the diaspora carries in both places, on top of an already high genetic burden of cardiovascular disease.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It May Not Be How Much You Move, but How Many Ways — Exercise Variety Is Linked to a Longer Life
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A large analysis finds that people who mix walking, lifting, cycling and other activities have lower death rates than those who rely on a single form of exercise — even after accounting for how much they do in total.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new analysis links variety in physical activity, not just total volume, to lower mortality
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Many in the Indian diaspora settle into one fitness rut — the daily treadmill walk, the weekend cricket match, the gym routine that never changes — so evidence that mixing activity types adds years, independent of how much you do, offers a practical, low-cost upgrade for busy NRI households trying to outrun the community’s high cardiometabolic risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Plant-Forward Mediterranean Diet Was Tied to a 26% Lower Heart-Disease Risk Over 20 Years, a Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Following more than 3,000 Greek adults for two decades, researchers found that those who ate the most vegetables, fruit, legumes, grains and fish had dramatically lower cardiovascular risk — while calorie-heavy diets light on lean meat fared worst.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A plant-forward Mediterranean diet of vegetables, legumes, grains and fish was tied to lower 20-year heart-disease risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: A plant-forward pattern built on vegetables, legumes, whole grains and fish maps closely onto traditional Indian vegetarian and coastal cooking — so for a diaspora whose diets have drifted toward calorie-dense, processed convenience food abroad, this 20-year evidence is a reminder that the heart-protective template may already sit in their own kitchens.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It Isn't Being Alone That Ages the Mind — It's Feeling Lonely, a 175,000-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Drawing on data from 18 countries, researchers found that the perception of loneliness, far more than simply living a solitary life, predicted faster cognitive decline and a shorter life — a distinction with real consequences for how families care for ageing parents.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A 175,000-person study across 18 countries found feeling lonely, more than living alone, tracks with faster cognitive decline (Openverse)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For Indian families spread across continents — children in the US or UK, parents back home — this study reframes the worry: a grandparent who lives alone but feels connected may fare far better than one surrounded by people yet quietly lonely, a nuance that should reshape how the diaspora thinks about long-distance caregiving.

carousel.title: After Nearly Two Years, India Reopens Its Doors to Bangladeshi Tourists
carousel.excerpt: From June 28, Bangladeshis can once again apply for Indian tourist visas at five centres across the country, ending a suspension that began amid the 2024 upheaval. The thaw is the clearest sign yet that ties between the two neighbours are mending.
carousel.image_caption: Tourists at the Taj Mahal in Agra. India will resume issuing tourist visas to Bangladeshi nationals from June 28, 2026, ending a nearly two-year suspension.
carousel.nri_angle: India's decision to resume tourist visas for Bangladeshi nationals from June 28, after a nearly two-year suspension, signals a thawing of relations that resonates across the eastern subcontinent's diaspora — families straddling the India-Bangladesh frontier, and the large Bangladeshi-origin communities in Britain, the US, Canada and the Gulf with relatives on both sides, can again plan the cross-border visits for weddings, funerals and reunions that had been tangled in geopolitics since 2024.

carousel.nri_angle: Indian engineers staff the inference, infra, and silicon teams at OpenAI, Broadcom, and TSMC's US operations — and a shift from buying Nvidia GPUs to designing custom chips reshapes which skills get hired and which get commoditized.

carousel.title: Meta Bets $900 Million on an Indian Fintech — and Hands an Indian Founder the Keys to WhatsApp
carousel.excerpt: Meta is investing about $900 million in Bengaluru-based CRED at a $4.5 billion valuation and has named its founder, Kunal Shah, the global head of WhatsApp — a twin move that signals how central India has become to the messaging giant's push into payments.

carousel.nri_angle: WhatsApp is the default communication tool binding the Indian diaspora to family back home, and the elevation of an Indian fintech founder with no Silicon Valley pedigree to run it — alongside a near-billion-dollar bet on an Indian startup — is both a marker of diaspora ascent in Big Tech leadership and a sign that the payments and commerce features NRIs use to send money and shop across borders are about to be reimagined from an Indian playbook.
